topic: ESR1 mutation and endocrine therapy resistance in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer
notes: Claims describe what the published literature asserts. No dataset, cohort, or outcome data was accessed at any point in constructing this graph.

claims.subject: E-001
claims.statement: Ligand-binding-domain mutations in ESR1 are recurrent in metastatic ER-positive breast cancer, occurring in 14 of 80 cases across two independent cohorts, with hotspots at Y537S, Y537N and D538G.

context.population: metastatic ER-positive breast cancer, two independent cohorts

claims.magnitude: 14/80 (17.5%) of metastatic ER-positive tumours carried ESR1 LBD mutations
claims.supporting_quote: We conducted a comprehensive genetic analysis of two independent cohorts of metastatic ER-positive breast tumors and identified mutations in ESR1 affecting the ligand-binding domain (LBD) in 14 of 80 cases. These included highly recurrent mutations encoding p.Tyr537Ser, p.Tyr537Asn and p.Asp538Gly alterations.

source.title: ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations in hormone-resistant breast cancer

claims.subject: E-001
claims.statement: ESR1 LBD-mutant receptors drive ER-dependent transcription and proliferation in the absence of hormone and reduce the efficacy of ER antagonists.

context.population: ER-positive breast cancer cell models expressing mutant ER

claims.supporting_quote: Consistent with this model, mutant receptors drive ER-dependent transcription and proliferation in the absence of hormone and reduce the efficacy of ER antagonists.
claims.mechanism_note: Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that the Tyr537Ser and Asp538Gly mutants form hydrogen bonds with Asp351, favouring the agonist conformation of the receptor (source-proposed).

source.title: ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations in hormone-resistant breast cancer

claims.subject: E-001
claims.statement: ESR1 LBD mutations were found only in patients previously treated with anti-estrogens and estrogen deprivation therapies, implicating prior endocrine exposure in their selection.

context.population: 11 patients with ER-positive metastatic breast cancer in a prospective clinical sequencing programme

claims.magnitude: 6/11 patients harboured ESR1 LBD mutations, all endocrine-pretreated
claims.supporting_quote: Whole-exome and transcriptome analysis showed that six cases harbored mutations of ESR1 affecting its ligand-binding domain (LBD), all of whom had been treated with anti-estrogens and estrogen deprivation therapies.

source.title: Activating ESR1 mutations in hormone-resistant metastatic breast cancer

claims.subject: E-001
claims.statement: Five LBD-localised ESR1 mutations conferred constitutive activity but retained responsiveness to anti-estrogen therapies in vitro.

context.population: engineered ER mutant constructs (L536Q, Y537S, Y537C, Y537N, D538G)

claims.supporting_quote: The five new LBD-localized ESR1 mutations identified here (encoding p.Leu536Gln, p.Tyr537Ser, p.Tyr537Cys, p.Tyr537Asn and p.Asp538Gly) were shown to result in constitutive activity and continued responsiveness to anti-estrogen therapies in vitro.
claims.mechanism_note: Constitutive, ligand-independent ER activity that can still be antagonised by direct receptor-binding agents is the mechanistic basis proposed for AI resistance with retained SERD/SERM sensitivity.

searched_and_not_found: No study found reporting somatic ESR1 LBD mutation prevalence or effect stratified by genetic ancestry or by self-reported race in HR+ metastatic breast cancer. Searches for African-ancestry / Black / Hispanic / East-Asian-specific somatic ESR1 mutation prevalence returned only germline ESR1 polymorphism and breast-cancer-risk literature (rs2234693, rs9349799), which is a different construct. This is a hard population gap.

No study found reporting ESR1 mutation prevalence or effect specifically in premenopausal versus postmenopausal patients. Nearly all pivotal trials (SoFEA, EFECT, EMERALD, PADA-1) enrolled predominantly postmenopausal women; premenopausal patients on ovarian function suppression are essentially uncharacterised.

No study found reporting ESR1 mutation effect stratified by de novo stage IV versus recurrent metastatic disease as an explicit interaction term. The closest is Schiavon 2015 (adjuvant-first vs metastatic-first AI exposure, C-009) and BCR 2020 (newly diagnosed metastatic, C-040), neither of which is a de novo/recurrent contrast.

No head-to-head randomised comparison found of any next-generation oral SERD versus fulvestrant restricted to a tissue-detected (rather than ctDNA-detected) ESR1-mutant population. Every registrational trial in this graph selected patients by ctDNA.

No study found that estimates the sensitivity of a tissue-only targeted NGS panel (e.g. MSK-IMPACT on archival primary tissue) for clinically relevant ESR1 mutations against a contemporaneous ctDNA reference in a large cohort. The one paired concordance study found (C-039) has n=43 and mutation-level concordance of only 44%.

No study found reporting whether ESR1 mutation detected on tissue sequencing carries the same treatment-interaction as ESR1 mutation detected on ctDNA. All predictive evidence (C-011, C-015, C-017, C-026, C-028) is ctDNA-derived; all tissue-derived evidence (C-035, C-036, C-037) is descriptive/prevalence, not predictive.

No large real-world overall-survival analysis found of ESR1-mutant versus wild-type patients with drug-level treatment sequencing that adjusts for line of therapy and duration of prior endocrine exposure. Existing OS claims (C-017, C-034) are small and conflict.
No study found on ESR1 mutation and outcome in male breast cancer.
No study found reporting the interaction between ESR1 mutation and specific CDK4/6 inhibitor identity (palbociclib vs ribociclib vs abemaciclib). SERENA-6 pooled all three.

No published randomised evidence found on whether ESR1 mutation status modifies benefit from chemotherapy or from antibody-drug conjugates in HR+ mBC; only a single small first-line paclitaxel/bevacizumab plasma study surfaced and was not verified.

No study after 2022 found with n > 500 that reports an ESR1-mutation-by-treatment interaction on survival in a tissue-sequenced cohort. C-031 (n=3958, Tempus) is the largest tissue+ctDNA analysis but reports enrichment, not an outcome interaction.
temporal_staleness: The foundational mechanistic claims (C-001 through C-004) rest on 2013 cohorts of n=80 and n=11 respectively and have not, to my knowledge, been re-derived at scale in a modern tissue-sequenced cohort.

The core predictive claim that ESR1 mutation selects for fulvestrant over exemestane (C-011, C-015, C-017) rests on retrospective biomarker analyses of trials that accrued 2004-2013, using fulvestrant 250 mg in EFECT and SoFEA, a dose now considered subtherapeutic.
The single most-cited null result (C-020, Spoerke 2016) has not been re-examined in the oral-SERD era.
ascertainment_caveats_for_tissue_sequenc: ESR1 LBD mutations are near-absent in treatment-naive primary tissue (0.16%, C-005) and 0% in tissue biopsies after adjuvant AI progression (C-010), but reach 30-48% in ctDNA of AI-pretreated metastatic patients (C-015, C-025). A tissue-panel cohort will therefore systematically under-ascertain ESR1 mutation status.
ESR1 mutations are frequently subclonal and polyclonal (C-018, C-019), which further reduces detection sensitivity on a bulk tissue panel with a limited variant allele frequency floor.

Timing of biopsy relative to AI exposure is the dominant determinant of detection (C-009). In a tissue cohort where most sequenced specimens predate or coincide with metastatic AI therapy, ESR1-mutant status will be strongly confounded with time-on-treatment and with the fact of having been re-biopsied at all.

Paired-sample work shows primary/metastasis discordance is near-total for ESR1 (C-038), so ESR1 status from an archival primary specimen should not be treated as the status of the treated metastatic disease.

Detected-ESR1-mutant patients in a tissue cohort are, by construction, enriched for long prior endocrine exposure. Any apparent association with survival is therefore confounded by immortal-time and by treatment-line depth. This is the prognostic-versus-predictive confusion flagged in the topic brief and it is live: C-017 and C-040 report worse outcome, C-034 reports none.
